correctness.rationale: For every prime power q≡7 mod12, −1 and 3 are nonsquares. The anisotropic norm-one conic T has q+1 points. For each nonzero peripheral sum s, the norm-one pair difference lies in the one-dimensional perpendicular line and yields at most one unordered peripheral pair; a possible center/peripheral collision would require a square root of 3 and is excluded. Thus the only exceptional convolution sum is zero. Fourier orthogonality then gives exact Q=2B²−D−2R+|c²+H|²+4|c|²B. Antipodal pair AM–GM, Cauchy–Schwarz and triangle bounds reduce the maximization to center squared mass y=3a²/2 and peripheral equal mass a², with aligned antipodal products. The six independent nonnegative exact deficit terms sum to the claimed sharp difference. Independently enumerated 7, 19, 31 prime conics, verified fiber multiplicities, unweighted energy, and rational sharp equality ratios. Prime-field enumeration does not prove all prime powers; the algebraic conic argument does.
